groups.description: Byte to vector embedding. Frozen in the online learner (no rule updates it yet).
Recurrent cell parameters (selected: gru, see model/specs/architecture.json); slow weights.

W_FAST (tensor memory.fast): short-lived associative matrix over sparse pattern-separated keys, written by a normalized delta rule with per-write decay; not persistent belief, never answers semantic queries.

W_MEMORY semantic keys: memory.semantic.keys (one unit-norm pooled key per slot, for the attention read) and memory.semantic.key_words (per-word vectors, for late-interaction verification). Produced by the frozen memory encoder at write time; zero when empty or erased.
W_MEMORY semantic values (memory.semantic.values): each value as rows of the frozen byte embedding, NUL-terminated; read by attention and decoded by nearest-embedding cleanup.

Frozen W_CORE memory encoders: core.memory_encoder (seeded random-feature embedding bag over hashed byte trigrams) and core.fast_separator (seeded projection for the k-winners-take-all W_FAST key). Verified byte-identical on every checkpoint load.
W_MEMORY metadata tensors (memory.semantic.meta, memory.state): status, confidence, logical creation/update time, source, provenance hash, supersession links, contradiction count; event clock.
Episodic ring (memory.episodic.keys, memory.episodic.meta): one record per memory operation (what happened), separate from semantic beliefs; key vectors are erased on forget.

Frozen vector-symbolic constants (core.reasoner.*): the atom hash table (core.reasoner.atom_table, input of the atom-encode circuit), the role phasors (subj, rel, obj, quant, scope) and relation atoms it computes, and the two fractional-power number tables (core.reasoner.number_digits, input of the number-encode circuit; core.reasoner.number_codebook, input of the number-decode circuit). Seeded; verified bit-identical on load.

Relational memory (memory.relations.*): one bound role-filler bundle per stated fact or rule, its polarity/confidence/provenance metadata, and the codebook of symbol vectors seen. Written only from user statements; derived answers are never written back.

Next-byte readout (readout.weight, readout.bias) over [GRU hidden ; last-byte embedding]. Starts at zero (uniform prediction); updated online by the delta or Hebbian rule with constants from model/specs/online-learning.json.

W_PROG: compiled circuit constants (tensors prog.<circuit>.<name>), produced by the zerolm-wsp compiler from model/prog/ specs with pinned hashes; verified bit-identical to the compiler output on every checkpoint load. Changed only by validated WSP patches (apply/revert, crates/zerolm-wsp/src/patch.rs); no circuit declares adaptable blocks yet.
Skill-level weight edits, accepted only via validated patches.
Frozen bounded grammar seed tables: lexical attributes, ordered rewrites, byte classes, and recognition templates with numeric frame readouts.

Representation-feasibility research arm (roadmap Gate A): a plastic copy of the byte embedding and the selected GRU core (tensors embed, gru.wz..gru.bh) changed by the candidate local rule (e-prop with fixed random feedback; eligibility traces are session state, not weights). The frozen core of the memory milestone is a separate copy and stays byte-identical. Research code only; not part of any checkpoint.

Mainline online-gradient learner (Gate A rerun, constitution invariant 4 as amended by research/decisions/gate-a-2026-11-26.md): the byte embedding, the selected GRU core, and a readout, trained in one chronological pass by truncated backpropagation through time with Adam; every update chunk is logged (input stream, signal, rule, changed tensors, checkpoint hash). Same seeded initialization as the other arms. Not part of any memory checkpoint; no offline pretraining.

Experiment GDM research arm (docs/gdm-experiment.md): one-head gated delta-rule fast-weight memory beside the gradient_core GRU: tables gdm.u, gdm.v, gdm.d (256 x 32), scalars gdm.a0, gdm.b0, gdm.gamma0 and gate vectors gdm.wa, gdm.wb, trained with the rest of the core by single-pass truncated backpropagation (every update logged, changed tensors named); the fast-weight state S (32 x 32) is persistent session state written by the gated delta rule, not a parameter. Initial value either a compiled content-independent code table (seed entry gdm-code-table) or seeded random rows. Research code only; not part of any checkpoint.
